source.title: MaskForge: Structure-Aware Adaptive Attacks for Jailbreaking Diffusion Large Language Models
source.authors: Ying-Zi Ma; Zheng-Yue Zhao; Xiaogeng Liu; Minhui Xue; Yue Zhao; Chao-Wei Xiao

page_placements.theme: Diffusion-language safety depends on positions and trajectories

record.tranche_reason: Tests a composite compliant-opening and mask-scaffold attack on diffusion LLMs, a different model setting from the claim’s original autoregressive focus; it reports harmful-compliance rates and tests an any-order safety defense.
record.gate_note: The paper reports attack success rates for MaskForge, which places an affirmative commitment in the victim’s assistant turn alongside a mask-bearing scaffold. This does not isolate the effect of the opening from the scaffold or other attack components. The paper also reports safety-defense and mask-ratio results. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, fine-tune the victim on small harmful or benign datasets, or test adversarial suffixes or decoding changes.
record.test_reason: MaskForge is a black-box attack on diffusion LLMs. Its template begins with the goal sentence, then an affirmative commitment line ("Here is the complete case study..."), then mask slots, prefilled into the assistant turn. It reports ASR against DIRECT baselines. That is a compliant start in a new model family, so it bears on V4, but only as a bundle with the scaffold and adaptive search. A2D, a different any-order training defence, is tested against it on one model, which bears loosely on V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that MaskForge, a structure-aware black-box mask-infilling attack, bypasses dLLM safety, transfers to AdvBench and unseen victims, and resists published defences such as A2D, with a safety surface unlike autoregressive prefix attacks. The paraphrase is accurate, but the paper does not claim the compliant opening alone causes the bypass.
record.recipe_differences: Black-box, adaptive mask-bearing scaffold attack on diffusion LLMs; no small-data fine-tuning, per-token KL analysis, or isolated compliant-opening intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies with victim, benchmark, retrieval strategy, and mask ratio; ASR rises on average as the mask ratio increases. Under A2D, the reported MaskForge-Embed ASR on Dream-Instruct falls from 94.0% to 85.0%.

fits_no_version.finding: Average ASR rises with the mask ratio of the attack template, from 62.0% at r=0.1 to 78.8% at r=0.9, on four diffusion LLMs (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion LLMs, mask-template structure and mask ratio affect harmful-completion attack success.

record.problems: ASR and harmfulness are judged by a single external model in the main evaluations; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper’s composite attack does not isolate the compliant opening from its mask scaffold, prompt framing, adaptive search, and other components.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports HarmfulScore values, the retrieval-strategy ablation in Table 9, fallback ablation in Table 6, and defense comparisons in Figures 3–4. These are not included because they do not isolate the compliant-opening effect or add a separate tested result for V7 beyond the Dream-Instruct A2D comparison; the mask-ratio ASR sweep and main attack ASRs are retained.

untested.parts: The opening is not isolated from the mask scaffold, and adversarial suffixes and decoding changes are not tested. Standalone prefill on a diffusion model is not reported.
The causes of shallowness are not tested.
Token-depth deepening is not tested. Only A2D and PO, which are any-order/random-masking SFT defences, are compared, and only on Dream-Instruct with one attack.

missing.what: Defence results for PAD and DIJA against A2D, PO and Self-reminder (e.g. Dream-Instruct A2D PAD 30, DIJA 26). They show the A2D defence works against fixed-template attacks but not MaskForge, which matters for V7 comparison.
Defence results for three other victims beyond Dream-Instruct, shown only in figures.
Utility cost of PO and A2D: average accuracy falls from 46.8 to 16.5 and 7.0.
Baseline ASR of the fallback ablation (full 75.2 vs no-fallback 74.3), not relevant to any version.

record.verdict_notes: The study's own method is the attack, so the V4 evidence is for a composite. The reader's baselines for r20 and r25 (MMaDA-CoT DIRECT 62.0) mean the state labels vary mostly by baseline level. The reader's second V4 limits_scope label rests on missing isolation of the opening, which is untested rather than a result, so it should be dropped. The paper cites prefix-centric alignment work but does not test V3, V5 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
The compliant opening is bundled with a mask-bearing scaffold; its independent effect is not isolated. Adversarial suffixes and decoding changes are not tested.
Localization of safety behavior in weights, parameters, or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Tests a reproduced A2D any-order/any-step defense against MaskForge on Dream-Instruct, but does not measure token-position depth or test other deepening methods.

rows.subject: Dream-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Frozen-library MaskForge-Embed attack against the base checkpoint
rows.note: Reference condition for the defended-checkpoint comparisons.
rows.check: This is the undefended reference at 94.0, not a deepening intervention. It should be kept only as a baseline for the V7 comparison.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix D, Table 8, Base, MaskForge-Embed ASR

rows.subject: Dream-Instruct + Self-reminder
rows.operation_detail: Frozen-library MaskForge-Embed attack with a system-level safety reminder
rows.note: Prompt-only defense; not itself a deepening-training intervention.
rows.check: Self-reminder is a prompt-only defence with no training, so it does not bear on V7.

rows.subject: Dream-Instruct + PO
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned with random-masking SFT on a refusal-augmented dataset
rows.operation_detail: Preference Optimization defense, followed by frozen-library MaskForge-Embed evaluation
rows.note: The paper describes PO as random-masking SFT, but not specifically as a test of spreading safety beyond first tokens.
rows.check: The paper describes PO as random-masking SFT on refusal data. It does not claim this spreads safety beyond the first tokens, so the link to V7 is weak. A drop from 94 to 87 is small.

rows.subject: Dream-Instruct + A2D
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned with random-masking SFT and any-order, any-step safety labels
rows.operation_detail: A2D defense, followed by frozen-library MaskForge-Embed evaluation
rows.note: A2D lowers the attack rate relative to base, but the attack still succeeds on 85.0%.
rows.check: A2D is any-order, any-step training, a different mechanism from deepening token depth. The drop from 94 to 85 is a small move in the right direction, which counts as partial. The reader's measure of 'partial' is acceptable.

relationships.condition: Diffusion LLMs (LLaDA, LLaDA 1.5, LLaDA2.0-mini, Dream, MMaDA) attacked with MaskForge, a composite attack that includes an affirmative assistant-turn opening
relationships.reason: ASR rises from near 0-27% (DIRECT) to 68-98% across HarmBench, StrongREJECT, JailbreakBench and AdvBench (r1-r25). The effect comes from the bundled attack, not the opening alone, per the study's design.
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose from about 0–27% with direct prompts to 68–98% across four benchmarks; the effect belongs to the bundled attack, not the opening alone.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Diffusion LLMs (LLaDA, LLaDA 1.5, LLaDA2.0-mini, Dream, MMaDA) attacked with MaskForge, a composite attack that includes an affirmative assistant-turn opening
source_check.reason: Tables 1–4 support bypass by the composite assistant-prefill attack described in Appendix G.1; they do not isolate the opening's contribution. The rationale's ranges need correction: DIRECT reaches 75.7% on MMaDA-CoT/StrongREJECT, and MaskForge-Goal reaches only 47.0% on LLaDA2.0-mini/AdvBench.

relationships.condition: Dream-Instruct with A2D defence under frozen-library MaskForge-Embed on JailbreakBench
relationships.reason: A2D lowers ASR only from 94.0% to 85.0% (r46, r49), so any-order alignment does not hold up against this attack. This is one model and one attack, and A2D is not a first-token deepening method.
relationships.display_finding: A2D lowered attack success only from 94.0% to 85.0%, in one model under one attack, and A2D is not a first-token deepening method.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Dream-Instruct with A2D defence under frozen-library MaskForge-Embed on JailbreakBench
source_check.reason: Table 8 confirms r46=94.0% and r49=85.0% ASR: the reproduced any-order, any-step training provides partial protection against this attack. This qualifies robustness of the diffusion deepening analogue without testing the original first-token deepening method.

relation.reason: The study measures harmful compliance against DIRECT controls and compares defended checkpoints with their undefended reference.

tranche.reason: Diffusion mask-infilling is a new setting with measured harmful compliance under assistant-turn prefilling and an any-order, any-step safety-training evaluation.

source_check.notes: Appendix D describes a reproduced random-masking SFT implementation of A2D; equivalence to the original implementation is not established. Table 8 also reports Dream-Instruct average utility falling from 46.8% to 7.0% under A2D.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MaskForge composite attacks on the tested diffusion LLMs and benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: MaskForge’s assistant-turn opening plus mask scaffold produces high ASR across the main benchmarks and AdvBench; this supports bypass by the composite attack, not an isolated opening effect (r1–r25).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Standalone compliant-opening effect and variation across tested victims/settings
reader_labels.reason: The opening is bundled with structural mask infilling, and ASR varies substantially by model and benchmark; the paper does not establish that the opening alone bypasses safety (r1–r25).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: A2D defense on Dream-Instruct under frozen-library MaskForge-Embed
reader_labels.reason: A2D reduces ASR from 94.0% to 85.0%, but does not prevent high attack success in this test (r46, r49).
